K1.stone_why: Sturdy wedge-serifed humanist with weight, but it reads as a bookish slab rather than lettering cut in stone.
K1.carving_why: Display titles and set numbers have smooth, ink-like curves; only the wedge serifs hint at a cut.
K1.calm_why: Even, grounded rhythm with no shouting, though the bold numbers are quite dark.
K1.personality_why: Warm, slightly condensed wedge serif with a distinct voice that suits a gentle tracker.
K1.inscription_why: Capitals are narrow and slab-like (BENCH PRESS, SISIFO), far from Roman inscriptional proportions.
K1.oblique_why: A true cursive italic with consistent slant and even colour, clearly distinct, slightly narrow at 13 px.
K1.small_why: 13 px lines are crisp and readable, a little compact in width.

K2.stone_why: A neutral grotesque sans with no lapidary quality at all.
K2.carving_why: Perfectly smooth, engineered curves at every display size.
K2.calm_why: Quiet and orderly, but the heavy bold numbers feel technical rather than grounded.
K2.personality_why: Competent but generic UI sans; nothing ties it to stone or Sisyphus.
K2.inscription_why: Monoline grotesque capitals have none of the Roman inscriptional stroke or proportion.
K2.oblique_why: Clean, consistent italic with true italic forms, clearly distinct and readable at 13 px.
K2.small_why: Very open, sharp and even at 13 px; the most comfortable small text of the set.

K3.stone_why: Clearly lapidary, Trajan-like capital letterforms evoke carved monuments.
K3.carving_why: Despite the inscriptional shapes the outlines are smooth and drawn, with no visible facets.
K3.calm_why: Dignified in plain titles, but the swash capitals and all-caps body become theatrical and busy.
K3.personality_why: Very memorable, but its movie-poster classicism risks overwhelming a quiet app.
K3.inscription_why: Regular capitals have true Roman proportions, though the swash variants (bold MOBILITÀ, italic SISIFO · ROCK) undercut the dignity.
K3.oblique_why: Italic small caps look like a mechanical skew and are hard to read as running emphasis.
K3.small_why: 13 px text sets entirely in small caps, which is tiring and unsuitable for body copy.

K4.stone_why: Rough, irregular outlines give a weathered, hand-cut stone feel.
K4.carving_why: Display titles and numbers show clear chiselled facets and broken, flat-cut curves.
K4.calm_why: The roughness creates a nervous, uneven texture and the bold lines barely differ from regular.
K4.personality_why: Strongly distinctive, ancient-feeling character with real imperfection.
K4.inscription_why: Capitals have classical proportions and a weathered inscription look, though somewhat irregular.
K4.oblique_why: Italic is distinct but a calligraphic, almost blackletter-tinged cursive that is busy and lumpy at 13 px.
K4.small_why: 13 px lines are readable but the ragged edges soften and the colour is uneven.

K5.stone_why: Faceted glyphic serif that reads convincingly as letters cut into stone.
K5.carving_why: SISIFO, the titles and 62.5 show crisp polygonal facets and flat-cut curves at display size.
K5.calm_why: Wide, steady rhythm with presence; the faceting adds texture without aggression.
K5.personality_why: Memorable chiselled character that fits the stone and engraving brief closely.
K5.inscription_why: Capitals (BENCH PRESS, MOBILITÀ · EQUILIBRIO) have broad Roman proportions and a dignified flared stroke.
K5.oblique_why: A real italic with consistent slant and even colour, clearly distinct, slightly light at 13 px.
K5.small_why: 13 px text is open and readable; the facets disappear at that size so it stays clean.

K6.stone_why: Heavy, angular old-style serif with a solid, grounded mass.
K6.carving_why: Some angular serifs and sheared terminals at display size, but the bowls stay mostly smooth.
K6.calm_why: Very dark colour throughout makes titles and numbers feel heavy and slightly loud.
K6.personality_why: Distinctive, robust and slightly quirky (the open g), though more bookish than lapidary.
K6.inscription_why: Capitals are solid and classical with good dignity, a little dense and heavy.
K6.oblique_why: True italic with steady slant, but whole italic lines run dark at 13 px.
K6.small_why: 13 px text is legible and sharp, if somewhat heavy in colour.

K7.stone_why: Elegant high-contrast serif that feels editorial rather than carved.
K7.carving_why: Smooth bracketed serifs and soft curves at display sizes, no facets.
K7.calm_why: Quiet and refined with an even rhythm.
K7.personality_why: Polished but close to a generic magazine serif.
K7.inscription_why: Capitals have classical proportions and decent dignity, with a slightly modern contrast.
K7.oblique_why: Well-formed true italic, consistent and distinct, readable at 13 px.
K7.small_why: 13 px text reads well, though the thin hairlines lighten it slightly.

K8.stone_why: Flared glyphic sans with inscriptional ancestry gives a quiet, chiselled-sans feel.
K8.carving_why: The flare is smooth and drawn; display letters show no cut facets.
K8.calm_why: Very calm, even and graceful with presence and no aggression.
K8.personality_why: Recognisable humanist-flared character that suits the app, if familiar.
K8.inscription_why: Capitals have Roman-derived proportions and flaring, a sans echo of inscriptional letters.
K8.oblique_why: A clean, evenly coloured sloped roman, consistent and readable, less distinct than a true italic.
K8.small_why: 13 px text is open, sharp and comfortable.

M1.stone_why: The 60 and 5 set numbers are visibly faceted and carved; the title is only faintly cut.
M1.hierarchy_why: Title, caps column heads, set rows and big steppers are distinct and the screen is orderly.

M2.stone_why: Title and 20 min figures read as a calm serif; the cut is barely perceptible at these sizes.
M2.hierarchy_why: Card label, value and detail lines separate clearly and the list stays quiet.

M3.stone_why: History title and card names show only a slight cut; there are no large numbers to carry it.
M3.hierarchy_why: Title, spaced-caps date headings, card titles and meta lines form a clear, calm order.

M4.stone_why: Large stepper numbers look chiselled; the title is solid with a slight cut.
M4.hierarchy_why: Roles are distinct and the rest timer button joins without clutter.

M5.stone_why: The title and especially the 60 and 5 show the crispest, most visible facets of the workout screens.
M5.hierarchy_why: Same clear structure: title, caps headers, set rows, stepper numbers and button all distinct.

M6.stone_why: Titles look marginally firmer than on the other History screen but still read mostly smooth.
M6.hierarchy_why: Clear, calm order of title, date headings, card titles and meta lines.

M7.stone_why: Faceted stepper numbers read as carved; the smaller title loses some of its cut.
M7.hierarchy_why: Tighter layout keeps roles distinct, though the smaller title has slightly less presence.

M8.stone_why: Numbers show clear facets and the smaller title a modest cut.
M8.hierarchy_why: Orderly and distinct roles in the compact layout, title a little understated.

M9.stone_why: Title and value lines are firm but read as a smooth serif at these sizes.
M9.hierarchy_why: Clear label, value, detail stacking within calm cards.

M10.stone_why: Stepper numbers are clearly faceted and the title shows a slight cut.
M10.hierarchy_why: Distinct roles and a calm layout with the rest timer integrated.
